review_type: Independent AI semantic audit; not human-validated. Frozen supplied sources only; no web verification of underlying allegations.
scope: All original 29 Putin main defense records, both Kim records and both MBS records; relevant full source exchanges and continuation reviewed. Targeted consistency screen of Canada/Mexico candidates, seven Putin sensitivity examples, MBS main and sensitivity evidence, and whole-corpus Khashoggi aliases. Not an independent exhaustive whole-corpus recall audit.
unit: Unique official DCPD communication × target, regardless of multiple passages.

rubric.main: Explicit adopted justification, normalization, personal-conduct/performance/reputation rebuttal, or direct protective/fairness defense of the leader. Allow mild diplomatic and protective defense, but mark subtype and significance.
rubric.exclude_main: State-only sympathy; affinity/praise alone; mere attributed rationale without adoption; generic peace intentions; claims own policy creates pressure; ambiguous causal prediction without secure normative function.
rubric.comparability: Counts use shared semantic boundary, not equivalence of moral significance, opportunities, exposure, misconduct severity or leaders’ underlying acts. Economic-performance rebuttal, protective fairness, diplomacy and murder denial are distinct subtypes.
rubric.truth_status: Codes what Trump asserted. Neither historical statistics nor alleged incidents nor denials are fact-checked by this audit.

initiation_summary_audited_main_passages.note: any_prompted includes an answer to any question, even an unrelated question. It can overlap any_unsolicited_target_introduction. For reporting, prefer the mutually exclusive observed_kind_counts and direct-target/conduct-prompt field.

mandatory_changes.reason: I understand it can refer to Ukraine hitting Putin after his attacks; not playing games is immediately explained as wanting all Ukraine, not necessarily favorable conduct. At 231 Trump faults Putin while also blaming others; this is insufficiently clear mitigation for secure main defense.

Gave Putin a reason to bomb and anticipated retaliation can be strategic causal explanation rather than endorsing a justified response. Keep literal evidence, but do not equate reason automatically with normative excuse.

Feeling pressure is a psychological/policy-effectiveness claim. Wanting the war ended is peace-intention rhetoric. Neither addresses, excuses or normalizes the reported attack on civilians; a critical prompt does not itself turn a favorable answer into defense.

source_evidence.speaker: Trump
source_evidence.quote: I love Canada. I love the people of Canada—many friends that live in Canada. But their leadership from Trudeau to the current leadership—I mean, in all fairness to them, they need us to survive. Without us, there's no way they can survive. So—but they've been very, very tough over a period of the last 50 years, actually.

consistency_checks.finding: No main personal defense from I do not blame them. Immediate antecedent is Canada taking industry and state trade policy; leaders are named later. Keep state-only mitigation separate rather than automatically back-projecting personal attribution.

source_evidence.speaker: Trump
source_evidence.quote: And people are surprised when I say it. Like, I have China coming here. A lot of people say: "Who's the toughest one to deal with? Is it China, sir? Is it China? Is it Vietnam? Is it"—I said, "No, actually, it's Canada." Canada has felt emboldened. We—they had Presidents that didn't know what was happening. Not only the last one, all of them. I mean, they just were taken into—our country's been taken advantage of by Canada.

source_evidence.speaker: Trump
source_evidence.quote: They took 20 percent of our car industry out. I don't blame them for that, but if we would have had a President that knew what was happening, nobody would have left. Now they're all coming back. All they would have had to do is charge tariffs, and they would have put tariffs on. If you build a car in Canada, you have to pay a 25-percent tariff, and nobody could pay. And if that didn't work, you make it 50 percent, or if that didn't work, you make it 100 percent.

source_evidence.speaker: Trump
source_evidence.quote: And we have everybody coming. Or you stop doing business with the nation. You know, when we lose $60- to $100 billion with Canada, I could say, "Well, if we don't do business"—because we don't need—we have more oil and gas than they do. We have tremendous forests. We don't need their lumber. We don't need the things they have. They need what we have. They do most of their business with us. I've heard numbers—95 percent. We do a very small percentage compared to others. We do a very small percentage by comparison to that.

source_evidence.speaker: Trump
source_evidence.quote: But they need us. We don't need them. They've taken advantage of us for years, and it's time to stop. We can't lose $60- to $100 billion a year for the privilege of allowing them to make cars. We don't want their cars. We want the cars to be made in Detroit and in South Carolina and in Tennessee and in all of our places where we make cars. We don't want them to be made in Canada. So this is nothing against anybody.

source_evidence.speaker: Trump
source_evidence.quote: And this started with Trudeau. Trudeau and I used to have it out pretty good, and now we have this new guy, who's a nice guy, but you know, he's just—and then they have the other guy, the slob. I guess some people call him a slob. I don't want to call him that because I want to be nice.
